verification.summary: The accs.bash has no timeout on curl or on waiting for the two background processes to come up, so a slow/hung mock-github or tracker start makes the whole check hang forever instead of failing — exactly what the dictionary says must be blocked. It also never checks that only active/open issues are shown, though the spec explicitly requires that filter.

mustFix.quote: IDS_T0="$(curl -sf "$API_URL" | ids_from_json)" || fail "mock GitHub API did not respond with issues at startup"
mustFix.problem: curl has no --max-time, and there's no overall script timeout, so if mock-github never comes up or hangs, this call blocks indefinitely instead of failing. That is the exact 'stuck forever' failure mode ACCS scripts must avoid.

shouldFix.problem: The ACCS never seeds or checks for a closed issue, so a tracker that prints closed issue numbers too would still pass. The 'active only' requirement from the man-made spec is effectively unverified.

shouldKnow.problem: Falling back to `.id` when `.number` is absent is an enrich-time assumption about the mock's JSON shape, not stated in the man-made prose. Fine as a documented flag, just worth the operator's eyes.

commits.subject: spec(reader): trim the prototype issues reader spec to the operator section and add accs.md
